STAGE 1 of a 4-stage pipeline on /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui.

YOUR JOB: independently VALIDATE OR DISPROVE five claims about test guards and token resolution, by EXECUTION. You are the proof stage — a later agent implements only what you confirm. Do NOT fix. Do NOT commit. Read-only except temporary probes you delete (end with a clean `git status`).

Allowed: `npx vitest run`, `npx tsx -e`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `node`, git reads, temporary probe files you delete.
FORBIDDEN: `npm start`, `npm run build-storybook`, `npx test-storybook` — another process owns those.

=== CLAIM S1 ===
`overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` — its three tests are all `expect(offenders).toEqual([])` over a `collect()` helper, and NOTHING asserts `collect()` actually found anything. Claim: if `theme/components/index.ts` ever changed export shape so `Object.entries(components)` yielded `[]`, all three tests would still pass and three regression guards written from three real shipped bugs would silently stop checking.
PROVE by: reading the test, then MUTATING the input so `collect()` returns empty (e.g. temporarily stub the import or empty the components map in a copy) and running vitest to show the tests still pass. That is the proof. Then confirm `expect(collect().length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` (or equivalent) fails under the mutation and passes normally.

=== CLAIM S3 ===
The same file's `walk()` helper reports the LEAF key as `prop`, so responsive forms are invisible to it:
  width: 'xl'              → CAUGHT
  _hover: {boxSize:'2xs'}  → CAUGHT
  width: ['xl','2xl']      → MISSED (passes '0'/'1' as prop)
  width: {base:'xl'}       → MISSED (passes 'base' as prop)
Claim: those missed forms are exactly the responsive idiom the project docs teach. Claim: one-line fix — carry the last non-index key forward as `prop`.
PROVE by: replicating `walk()` against those four synthetic inputs and reporting actual results. Then prove the proposed fix catches all four WITHOUT introducing false positives (test it against legitimate nested structures that must NOT be flagged — e.g. `_hover`, `_focusVisible`, and a genuine array of non-scale values).

=== CLAIM S4 ===
The documented `theme.sizes` fallthrough trap has an UNDOCUMENTED, UNGUARDED twin on typography: `theme.fontSizes` and `theme.lineHeights` are Chakra defaults, and the Zimmermann scale is NOT registered there. So a bare `fontSize: '2xs'` renders 0.625rem instead of the intended 0.875rem, and `fontSize: '4xs'` resolves to `undefined` and emits nothing.
PROVE by: importing the real theme and printing `theme.fontSizes` / `theme.lineHeights` / `theme.sizes` keys and values; demonstrate the divergence numerically for md/xs/2xs/3xs/4xs. Then confirm whether the branch currently has ANY bare-key usage on fontSize/lineHeight/letterSpacing (I believe zero — verify). Then confirm `recipeGuards.test.ts` does NOT guard these properties. Assess whether extending its SIZING_PROPS-style check to fontSize/lineHeight/letterSpacing is sound, and prove it catches a synthetic violation.
ALSO verify this related correction: is the `sizes` blow-up uniformly "20-30x"? Check `2xs` (claimed 64x: 0.25rem→16rem) and `s`/`m`/`l` (claimed ABSENT from sizes, so the declaration is dropped entirely rather than blown up).

=== CLAIM S2 ===
`overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx` — the `SubscribePlaceholder` play compares footer/slot heights before and after submit but never asserts either is non-zero, so if the story container ever collapsed, `0 === 0` would pass and the only guard on `subscribeControl`'s `minHeight` would stop guarding.
PROVE by: reading the assertion, then reasoning about (and if you can, demonstrating) whether a collapsed container actually yields 0 for both. Note: you CANNOT run test-storybook. So prove it by construction/logic plus any DOM measurement you can do against the running dev server at http://localhost:3000 (read-only page loads are fine, Playwright is available at node_modules/playwright-core). State clearly what you proved by execution vs by reasoning.

=== CLAIM S11 ===
`overrides/app/theme/components/footer.ts` `SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT = '2.8125rem'` states in its own comment that it is DERIVED from `overrides/app/theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '36px'` ("36px content + 4px/4px padding + 1px border"), and chose rem for WCAG 1.4.4 scaling. Claim: the two halves of one measurement use opposite units, so at 200% text zoom the rem slot doubles while the px content height does not, and the derivation stops holding.
PROVE by: measuring the actual rendered heights at default zoom and at an emulated larger root font-size / zoom against the dev server (Playwright can set deviceScaleFactor or you can inject a root font-size change). Show whether the field and the reserved slot diverge, and by how much. If they DON'T diverge in practice, say so — the claim would then be theoretical.

FOR EACH: **CONFIRMED** / **DISPROVED** / **PARTIALLY CONFIRMED**, with commands and output as evidence, and the minimal fix if confirmed. Distinguish what you proved by execution from what you inferred. A disproved claim is valuable — do not manufacture confirmation.

End with `git status --porcelain` proving the tree is clean.

# STAGE 1 VALIDATION REPORT

Environment: branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`, vitest 3.2.7, playwright-core 1.60.0, dev server live at `localhost:3000`. Note: another agent rewrote the branch history mid-run (HEAD moved from `564ff99` to `9ec0740`); I re-verified all five findings against current HEAD afterwards — all hold.

---

## CLAIM S1 — vacuous `collect()` guards: **CONFIRMED** (by execution)

**Baseline:** 3/3 pass.

**Mutation** (`components` replaced with `{}` in a copy of the test):
```
✓ overrides/app/theme/components/__probeS1.test.ts (3 tests) 1ms
Test Files 1 passed (1) | Tests 3 passed (3)
```
All three guards pass against an empty input. Because every assertion is `expect(offenders).toEqual([])`, an empty `collect()` satisfies all three trivially. Test 3 is vacuous the same way — `Object.keys(components).filter(...)` over `{}` is `[]`.

**Proposed guard, under mutation:**
```
AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 0   <- collect().length
AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 0   <- Object.keys(components).length
Tests 2 failed | 3 passed (5)
```
**Un-mutated control:** `COLLECT_COUNT 441 RECIPES 6 Button,ZimmFooter,Header,ListMenu,ZimmNavItem,ZimmTextInput` — guard passes.

**Minimal fix** — add to `describe('recipe guards')` in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`:
```ts
test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes', () => {
  expect(Object.keys(components).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(collect().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```
A floor of `> 0` is enough; don't pin 441 or 6 (churns on every legitimate recipe edit).

---

## CLAIM S3 — `walk()` reports the leaf key: **CONFIRMED**, but the **proposed fix is insufficient**

The four-case claim is exactly right (executed against `walk()` copied verbatim):

| input | current `walk()` |
|---|---|
| `width: 'xl'` | **CAUGHT** |
| `_hover: {boxSize:'2xs'}` | **CAUGHT** |
| `width: ['xl','2xl']` | **MISSED** |
| `width: {base:'xl'}` | **MISSED** |

Extended to 8 should-catch shapes, the current walker misses 6: both responsive forms, plus `_hover:{width:['xl']}`, `maxW:[null,'xl']`, `width:{base:'100%',md:'xl'}`, and a media-query-nested responsive object.

Both missed forms are the documented idiom — `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:17` teaches `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}` and line 123 teaches `['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`.

**Where the claim is wrong:** "carry the last non-index key forward" only fixes the **array** form. Responsive-object keys (`base`, `md`) are not numeric indices, so `width: {base:'xl'}` still escapes — 3 of 18 cases still wrong. Verified by execution.

**What actually works** — treat a node as a responsive *container* (array, or an object whose keys are *all* breakpoint names) and carry the enclosing property through it. Scored **0 incorrect of 18**, including 10 deliberate false-positive controls (`_hover`, `_focusVisible`, `transition` arrays, `fontFamily` stacks, `gridTemplateAreas`, `var()` values, `width:['100%','50%']`, and Chakra's own `sizes: {md:..., lg:...}` recipe shape which *must not* be misread as responsive):

```ts
const BREAKPOINT_KEYS = new Set(['base', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl', '2xl']);
const isResponsiveContainer = (n: object): boolean =>
  Array.isArray(n) || (Object.keys(n).length > 0 && Object.keys(n).every((k) => BREAKPOINT_KEYS.has(k)));

const walk = (node: unknown, recipe: string, path: string, hit: (f: Found) => void, prop = ''): void => {
  if (node === null || typeof node !== 'object') return;
  const responsive = isResponsiveContainer(node as object);
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(node as Record<string, unknown>)) {
    const here = path ? `${path}.${key}` : key;
    const p = responsive ? prop : key;              // <- the actual fix
    if (value !== null && typeof value === 'object') walk(value, recipe, here, hit, p);
    else if (typeof value === 'string') hit({ recipe, path, prop: p, value });
  }
};
```
The breakpoint-set check (not a per-key check) is load-bearing: `xl`/`2xl` are keys in *both* `breakpoints` and `spacing`, so only "are **all** keys breakpoints?" disambiguates.

**Against the real theme:** identical entry count (441), identical offender list (`[]`), and exactly 6 prop reassignments — all in the only 2 responsive shapes that exist today, both `var()`-valued so neither walker flags them:
```
Header.logoBar.paddingTop    ["var(--zimm-scale-xs)","var(--zimm-scale-xs)","var(--zimm-scale-m)"]
Header.logoBar.paddingBottom ["var(--zimm-scale-3xl)","var(--zimm-scale-3xl)","var(--zimm-scale-1200)"]
```
**Zero false positives.** The gap is currently latent, not live.

---

## CLAIM S4 — undocumented typography twin: **CONFIRMED** (by execution)

`theme/index.ts:52-58` registers `borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, space, textStyles, components` — `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` are exported from `foundation/index.ts` but **never registered**.

Actual emitted CSS (rendered through `ChakraProvider` with the real theme):

| declaration | emitted CSS | result |
|---|---|---|
| `fontSize: '2xs'` | `font-size: var(--chakra-fontSizes-2xs)` | **0.625rem (10px)**, intended 0.875rem (14px) |
| `fontSize: '4xs'` | `{ }` | **nothing emitted** |
| `lineHeight: '2xs'` / `'md'` | `{ }` | nothing emitted |
| `letterSpacing: 'footer'` / `'2xs'` | `{ }` | nothing emitted |

Both halves of the claim are numerically exact. Full divergence: `md` 16px vs 24px, `xs` 12px vs 16px, `2xs` 10px vs 14px, `3xs` 7.2px vs 12px (4 collisions, matching `theme/index.ts`'s own comment), `4xs` absent.

Worth distinguishing: **`fontSizes` has genuine wrong-value collisions** (silently plausible-but-wrong render). `lineHeights` and `letterSpacings` have **zero key overlap** with Chakra's, so those only ever drop the declaration — same class of bug, less deceptive symptom.

### Sub-question: is the `sizes` blow-up uniformly 20-30x? **No — claim's correction CONFIRMED**

Measured range **8.0x–112.0x**, and three keys aren't blown up at all:

## CLAIM S11 — mixed units break the derivation: **CONFIRMED** (measured, not theoretical)

`footer.ts:38` `SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT = '2.8125rem'` derives from `zimmTextInput.ts:27` `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '36px'`. At 100% the derivation is exact — measured field: content **36** + padding **4/4** + border **1px** = **45**, slot minHeight **45px**. 

The two halves then diverge, measured in Chromium by varying root font-size:

```
root  zoom | slot minH | slot H | field H | content H (minH) | pad T/B | bb  | GAP
16px  100% | 45px      | 45     | 45      | 36 (36px)        | 4px/4px | 1px |  0.00
20px  125% | 56.25px   | 56.25  | 47      | 36 (36px)        | 5px/5px | 1px |  9.25
24px  150% | 67.5px    | 67.5   | 49      | 36 (36px)        | 6px/6px | 1px | 18.50
32px  200% | 90px      | 90     | 53      | 36 (36px)        | 8px/8px | 1px | 37.00
```

At 200% the slot doubles (45→**90**) while the field reaches only **53** — a **37px** divergence. The field grows solely via its rem `2xs` padding; the 36px content and 1px border are frozen.

**Important refinement of the claim's framing:** the slot's rem choice is *correct*. The state it exists to reserve for — the result message — scales perfectly, and the slot tracks it proportionally at every zoom (slack is a constant 0.5625rem):
```
root  | slot H | msg H | msg lines | slack
16px  | 45     | 36    | 2 @18px   |  9.00
20px  | 56.25  | 45    | 2 @22.5px | 11.25
24px  | 67.5   | 54    | 2 @27px   | 13.50
32px  | 90     | 72    | 2 @36px   | 18.00
```
So the defective half is **`FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '36px'`**, not the slot. Consequences: because both states stay *under* the slot at every zoom (72 ≤ 90, 53 ≤ 90), the no-layout-shift guarantee still holds — this is **over-reservation (up to 37px of dead space around the field at 200%), not clipping or reflow**. The functional break is absent; what breaks is the derivation and therefore the accuracy of `footer.ts:33-34`'s comment at any zoom but 100%.

**Minimal fix:** `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '2.25rem'` (= 36px at default root) in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts:27`. Then at 200%: 72 + 16 + 1 = 89 vs slot 90 — derivation restored at all zoom levels, 1px residue being the deliberately-px border. Both files are Tier 2 (`theme/components/`, owner UI Designer — notify before changing), and the slot is already flagged PROVISIONAL pending Kiera, so this should ride along with that sign-off rather than landing silently.
